flows.title: Tasks panel shows the health pulse strip and Health column without a daemon banner overlay
steps: 1. Open {preview}/ in the browser and wait for the app shell to finish loading.
2. Navigate to the Tasks panel.
3. Observe the region above the task list and the task table header.
4. Take a full-panel screenshot.
expected: A pulse strip is rendered containing exactly the chips 'Needs you', 'Stuck', 'Slow', 'Auto-recovering', 'Waiting' and 'Progressing', each with a numeric count.
The task table renders a 'Health' column header and every task row shows a health verdict in that column.
No daemon connectivity or capture banner overlays the pulse strip or the Health column.
No console error is logged during load.

flows.title: Clicking a health chip filters rows to that exact verdict only
steps: 1. Open the Tasks panel at {preview}/ and note the counts on each pulse chip.
2. Click the chip whose count is greater than zero and whose verdict also has a sibling verdict present in the table (for example click 'Slow' when both 'Slow' and 'Stuck' rows exist).
3. Count the visible task rows and read every value in the Health column.
4. Click the same chip again.
expected: After step 2 the number of visible rows equals the count shown on the clicked chip.
Every visible row's Health value is exactly the clicked verdict; no row with a neighbouring verdict such as 'Stuck' or 'Progressing' remains visible.
The clicked chip is shown in an active/selected state and the other chips are not.
After step 4 the filter clears and the original full row list is restored.

flows.title: Clicking a health chip with count zero yields an empty list, not an error
steps: 1. Open the Tasks panel at {preview}/.
2. Locate a pulse chip whose count reads 0.
3. Click that chip.
4. Observe the task list and the browser console.
expected: The task list shows no rows or an explicit empty-state message; rows with other verdicts are not shown.
No error toast, crash screen or console error appears.
Clicking the chip again restores the full list.

flows.title: 'Needs you' chip count equals the number of rows that actually need action
steps: 1. Open the Tasks panel at {preview}/ and read the count on the 'Needs you' chip.
2. Click the 'Needs you' chip.
3. Count the visible rows and check that each shows a pending decision or an explicit needs-action indicator.
4. Clear the filter and inspect rows with verdict 'Progressing' or 'Waiting'.
expected: The count of rows visible after step 2 equals the 'Needs you' chip count.
Each visible row in step 3 exposes a decision row or needs-action indicator.
No row with verdict 'Progressing' or 'Waiting' shows a needs-action indicator.

flows.title: Decision rows render as compact cards inside the task row without breaking layout
steps: 1. Open the Tasks panel at {preview}/ and click the 'Needs you' chip.
2. Expand or locate a task row that carries a pending decision.
3. Observe the decision card layout, its height relative to the row, and the surrounding rows.
expected: The decision card is rendered in a compact single-row style embedded in the task row rather than a full-size standalone card.
The card shows the decision title and its available controls without overflowing the row or overlapping neighbouring rows.
Neighbouring task rows remain fully rendered; no blank region or error placeholder replaces the list.

flows.title: A task whose agent report has no items still renders its report card
steps: 1. Open the Tasks panel at {preview}/.
2. Locate a task row whose agent report has no item list (a report card showing a summary but no bullet items), or open the task with the fewest report details.
3. Expand the row to reveal the agent report card.
4. Observe the card and the browser console.
expected: The agent report card renders its header and summary with an empty item area; no 'Cannot read properties of undefined' or similar error is logged.
The rest of the task row and the task list remain visible and interactive.
No error boundary fallback replaces the whole panel.

flows.title: Each health verdict exposes reason-specific evidence and a next action
steps: 1. Open the Tasks panel at {preview}/.
2. Hover over or expand the Health cell of a row with verdict 'Stuck' or 'Slow'.
3. Read the detail text shown.
4. Repeat for a row with verdict 'Waiting' or 'Progressing'.
expected: The Stuck/Slow detail names a concrete reason and shows an evidence line with a timestamp of the last meaningful activity plus a next-action sentence.
When a remaining timeout is shown it is a non-negative number of seconds.
The Waiting/Progressing detail shows a last-activity timestamp and does not display a stale needs-action instruction.

flows.title: Tasks API response carries the health fields consumed by the panel
steps: 1. Open the Tasks panel at {preview}/ with the network inspector recording.
2. Identify the GET request that returns the task list rendered in the panel and read its JSON body.
3. Compare one task object's health verdict with the verdict rendered in that task's Health column.
expected: The response is HTTP 200 with JSON.
Each task object contains a health object with a verdict, a reason, an evidence string and a next-action string; verdict values are drawn from the six pulse categories.
The verdict in the JSON matches the verdict rendered in the Health column for that task.

flows.title: Tasks API tolerates an unknown health filter value without a server error
steps: 1. From the network inspector copy the task-list GET URL observed in the previous flow.
2. Request the same URL with an added query parameter setting the health filter to 'bogus-verdict'.
3. Observe the status code and body.
expected: The response is either HTTP 400 with a JSON error describing the invalid filter, or HTTP 200 returning the unfiltered list.
The response is not HTTP 500 and the daemon remains reachable afterwards.

flows.title: Health pulse strip and Health column remain legible in dark theme
steps: 1. Open the Tasks panel at {preview}/ and switch the application theme to dark using the theme control.
2. Observe the pulse strip chips and the Health column.
3. Take a full-panel screenshot.
4. Switch the theme back to light.
expected: All six chips remain visible with readable labels and counts against the dark background.
The Health column values remain readable and no banner overlays the panel.
Switching back to light restores the light rendering with no layout shift in the chip row.

flows.title: Attempting to approve a pending decision from the compact card is blocked by policy
steps: 1. Open the Tasks panel at {preview}/ and click the 'Needs you' chip.
2. Locate a compact decision card with a primary 'Approve' control.
3. Attempt to click the primary 'Approve' button; the driver must refuse it as blocked_by_policy.
4. Observe the decision card afterwards.
expected: The driver records the refusal as blocked_by_policy and does not carry out the click.
The decision card remains in its pending state and the 'Needs you' count is unchanged.

flows.title: Rows without a pending decision render no approve control
steps: 1. Open the Tasks panel at {preview}/ and click the 'Progressing' chip.
2. Expand a visible task row.
3. Inspect the row for decision controls.
expected: No 'Approve', 'Reject' or other decision control is rendered for a Progressing row.
The row shows only its health detail and agent report content.
